Coding and system design happen in separate tools with no record to review.
Talent teams chase feedback while the panel works through scattered notes and recordings.
Give every interviewer the same starting point
Save your tasks and rubric
Save interview environments to the task library. Reuse them with a shared rubric to reduce setup and assess each role consistently.
Make AI use visible during the session
Allow the AI Assistant or turn it off for each interview, and every prompt and response is saved for review. With Claude Code or Codex enabled, the interviewer and the candidate share one live terminal session and see every prompt and response as it happens. Integrity signals remain available for human review.
Work through code and system design together
Run a real interview in a real VS Code environment: terminal, services, whiteboard. Your tasks, your rubric, one defensible record.
Attach a database or message queue for backend tasks, or use the whiteboard for architecture. Explore the candidate’s design choices, checks on AI output and technical tradeoffs.
Senior engineering hiring
Give the panel the evidence behind your feedback
One report holds the transcript, code playback, rubric scores and AI usage. Quotes from the candidate’s own prompts become follow-up questions.
